To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an algorithm for the automatic segmentation of a shape, represented by a point cloud, into a minimal number of parts, that are consistent with the geometric characterization of a part.

1. we introduce a new method for shape segmentation that directly optimizes the decomposition based on an approximate convexity analysis, which is designed to handle both complete and incomplete shapes; 2. the segmentation is based on a non-local geometric signature that is computed based on the approximate convex components of the shape; 3. the segmentation is robust to missing regions and yields results that are similar to state-of-the art techniques on complete shapes; 4. the segmentation is fast and scalable, and
we present a shape segmentation technique that is robust to missing data, and is able to handle incomplete shapes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new shape analysis framework that is based on a novel segmentation technique.
the development of a segmentation method for shapes, which is based on the geometric properties of the shape and is robust to incomplete shapes.
the following questions: How can we decompose a shape based on its geometric structure?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the first to combine a complete shape decomposition method with an efficient and robust treatment of missing regions.
the proposed method can segment a shape into parts that are consistent with its geometry.
our approach is robust to noise, missing data and outliers, and it is able to handle incomplete shapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a method for shape segmentation that works for incomplete shapes.
we have a shape segmentation technique that is able to handle both complete and incomplete shapes and is able to produce results that are comparable with the state of the art.
the segmentation is based on a characterization, and that the method is robust to missing regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry of the expected parts in a shape can be used to drive the segmentation.
approximate convexity can be used to segment shapes in a robust and principled manner.
the geometry of a part can be described by a simple geometric signature, which can be used to segment the shape.
